title: An upgrade reducer must patch state and initialState together or replay fails with a hash mismatch
content:
The upgrade runs exactly **once**, when `UPGRADE_DOCUMENT` is dispatched. Replay never re-runs it: loading a document (`baseLoadFromInput` → `replayDocument`) starts from the stored `initialState` and folds the domain operations through the latest reducer. The `document`-scope log where the upgrade was recorded is not part of that fold.

That asymmetry is the whole trap. A migration that patches `state` but forgets `initialState` produces a document that looks perfectly healthy in the running system — and is unrecoverable:

- anything seeded into `initialState`, i.e. data that was never created by an operation, is still v1-shaped there;
- so a rebuild can no longer reproduce the stored state;
- so the replayed final state fails the recorded hash check.

The document then errors on load with a `HashMismatchError` whose message embeds `Hash mismatch on document …, scope global`. The recipe's tests match it with `/Hash mismatch/`.

The failure mode is worth dwelling on: nothing goes wrong at upgrade time, nothing goes wrong while the process stays up, and the break surfaces later on a cold load or on a peer that never held the live document. The `document-versioning` recipe ships a deliberately broken state-only transition specifically so the failure is visible in a test rather than in production.

Two supporting constraints from the same recipe. Upgrade reducers **must be pure** — they run on every peer that loads the document, so no `Date.now()`, no randomness, no I/O — and they must **return** a new document spread-style, because there is no immer/Mutative draft in an upgrade reducer and in-place mutation is simply lost. And `supportedVersions` is ordered and every hop must be covered: upgrading a v1 document on a package already at v3 composes v1→v2 then v2→v3, with a missing intermediate entry throwing at upgrade time.

Provenance: academy `05-Lookup/00-Cookbook.md`, Document Versioning recipe ("Critical pitfall: patch state and initialState together"), academy 6.2.2-dev.45.
description: Replay folds domain ops from the stored initialState and never re-runs the upgrade, so a state-only migration leaves v1-shaped seed data and the document errors on load.
